newsitem.title: USA: Continental seeks 24-hour talks with pilots.
newsitem.headline: Continental seeks 24-hour talks with pilots.

text.p: Continental Airlines Inc said Friday it wants "round-the-clock" negotiations with its pilots union and complained that the union's demand for pilot expense increases would cost $1.4 billion over three years.
The airline said the demand would "end this era of profitability."

"While you have been quick to criticize the company's economic proposal, your demand of a 100 percent increase to pilot expense would cost $1.4 billion over three years," the company said in a letter to Independent Association of Continental Pilots president Len Nikolai.

"Even your financial expert agrees that our assessment is accurate," the letter said. " It would end this era of profitability and plunge us back into the crisis mode that we only recently have escaped.

"More simply, it would stop cold the momentum of the Go Forward plan and therefore punish the pilots you represent, the other 34,200 employees, our shareholders and our customers," the letter continued.

On Thursday, the pilots union said it did not expect the negotiations to be finished by the previous July 1 target date. The pilots said they were setting Oct. 1 as the new date for reaching a contract.
The union and airline have been in talks since April 2, Continental said.
The airline said the only issues remaining to be resolved related to salary, benefits and expenses; and staffing and scheduling.
The union represents 4,000 pilots flying for Continental and about 1,000 flying for Continental Express.
